title: The derived subgroup is characteristic over every base algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Group schemes, closed normal subgroups, smoothness, connectedness and finite type have the meanings of [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type. Let $D(H)\subseteq H$ be the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ factors, as constructed in [lem-sfb-derived-commutator-word-arbitrary-field]. For a commutative $k$-algebra $A$, put $H_A=H\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $D(H)_A=D(H)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $A$-group-scheme automorphism $u:H_A\xrightarrow{\sim}H_A$, its restriction is an automorphism of the closed subgroup scheme $D(H)_A$; equivalently $u(D(H)_A)=D(H)_A$ as closed subgroup schemes of $H_A$. An $A$-group-scheme automorphism means an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ preserving multiplication, identity and inverse. The algebra $A$ need not be reduced, a field or of finite type.

source.place: Corollary 6.19(e) and its proof, printed pp.129--130, using the faithfully flat point description in 6.19(c). Characteristic here explicitly means invariance after every commutative base algebra, not only under k-automorphisms. No Stacks tag states this algebraic-group result.

proof.text: Put $X=H\times_kH$, $o=(e,e)$ and $c(x,y)=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$. The source $X$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and finite type by base change followed by composition in [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The group identities give $c(o)=e$ and $c(x,y)^{-1}=c(y,x)$ over every $k$-algebra. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] to this pointed inverse-stable map. With $P=k[H]$, $B_n=k[H^{2n}]$, $w_n=\prod_{i=1}^n[x_i,y_i]$ and $I=\bigcap_{n\ge1}\ker(w_n^*:P\to B_n)$, it identifies the smallest closed commutator subgroup with $\operatorname{Spec}C$, where $C=P/I$. This is precisely $D(H)$ of [lem-sfb-derived-commutator-word-arbitrary-field], by their identical minimality property. Write $q:P\twoheadrightarrow C$ and $f_n:C\to B_n$, so $f_nq=w_n^*$. These maps jointly detect zero: if every $f_n(q(p))=0$, then $p\in I$ by the displayed definition, hence $q(p)=0$.

source.place: Propositions 2.46 and 6.18; coordinate description after Corollary 6.19, printed pp.54–55,129–130

proof.text: Fix any commutative $k$-algebra $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], put $P_A=P\otimes_kA=k[H_A]$, $C_A=C\otimes_kA=k[D(H)_A]$ and $B_{n,A}=B_n\otimes_kA=k[(H_A)^{2n}]$. The identifications of the iterated products follow from the same fibre-product universal property. Their ring maps are $q_A=q\otimes1$ and $f_{n,A}=f_n\otimes1$, as checked on $p\otimes a$. The map $q_A$ is surjective: each element of $C_A$ is a finite sum $\sum_i c_i\otimes a_i$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and choosing $p_i$ with $q(p_i)=c_i$ gives the preimage $\sum_i p_i\otimes a_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection] with $M=C$, $N=A$, $J=\{1,2,\ldots\}$ and the maps $f_n$. It says that $f_{n,A}(t)=0$ for every $n$ implies $t=0$ in $C_A$. Its hypotheses hold because $A$ is a vector space over the field $k$ and step 1 gives zero detection on $C$.

source.place: Corollary 6.19(e), printed p.130: agent coordinate-ring argument using Proposition 2.46 instead of the faithfully-flat point description

proof.text: Let $u:H_A\to H_A$ be the given automorphism and let $u^*:P_A\to P_A$ be its $A$-algebra automorphism. On each test $A$-algebra, preservation of multiplication and inverse gives $u(\prod_i[x_i,y_i])=\prod_i[u(x_i),u(y_i)]$. Equivalently, with $U_n=u^{\times2n}$, $u\circ w_{n,A}=w_{n,A}\circ U_n$. These are identities of morphisms: their formulas already hold at the universal tuple with coefficient algebra $B_{n,A}$, using the affine morphism description [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Pulling back gives $f_{n,A}q_Au^*=U_n^*f_{n,A}q_A$. If $z\in\ker q_A$, the right side vanishes at $z$ for every $n$. Step 2 therefore implies $q_Au^*(z)=0$. Thus $\ker q_A$ is stable under $u^*$. Define $\bar u^*:C_A\to C_A$ by $\bar u^*(q_A(p))=q_A(u^*(p))$. Surjectivity of $q_A$ and stability of its kernel make this well defined and an $A$-algebra map. Its spectrum is a morphism $v:D(H)_A\to D(H)_A$ with $j_Av=uj_A$, where $j_A$ is the inclusion. This is factorization through the given closed subgroup as schemes, with all nilpotent functions retained.

source.place: Corollary 6.19(e), printed p.130: the commutator identity, written on coordinate algebras

proof.text: Apply step 3 also to $u^{-1}$ and obtain $v':D(H)_A\to D(H)_A$ with $j_Av'=u^{-1}j_A$. Then $j_Avv'=j_A$ and $j_Av'v=j_A$. Cancel $j_A$: on coordinate rings this is cancellation after the surjection $q_A$, so both composites are the identity by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus $v$ is an automorphism. It preserves the group operations because its composite with $j_A$ is the group homomorphism $uj_A$; for each $A$-algebra $R$, $D(H)_A(R)\to H_A(R)$ is injective since an algebra map out of $C_A$ is determined by its composite with $q_A$. Multiplication, identity and inverse identities for $v(R)$ follow by that injection. Finally $uj_A=j_Av$ and the analogous identity for $u^{-1}$ show $u(D(H)_A)=D(H)_A$ as closed subgroup schemes. The argument also covers $A=0$, where all the affine base changes are empty.
